t: AI, Amnesia, and the Art of the Chisel-Strike: Why WET Beats DRY
s: This article argues for the WET (Write Everything Twice) coding philosophy over DRY (Don't Repeat Yourself) when working with stateless, 'amnesic' AI models. It posits that providing explicit, repeated context ('rendering out') is more effective than relying on abstract, reusable logic for AI comprehension and task execution.
sub: WET vs. DRY coding philosophies for AI interaction
Thermodynamics of Human Energy and Productivity
Metaphors for managing complexity: Chisel-strikes, Zeno's Paradox, Rabbit Holes
